text:
If you like your outdoor plans dry, get them done before this afternoon. It's a bright, warm start, climbing toward a high near 86, but the same pop-up shower and thunderstorm risk everyone's flagging kicks in this afternoon into evening, mostly hit-or-miss and mainly favoring the higher terrain, though a stray cell could drift into town. The official call keeps odds low around 20 to 30 percent, but the European model is running much wetter than the American one today, so if you do get caught under one, it could dump hard for a few minutes. Ozone's up a bit today too, so if you're sensitive, don't overdo the midday exertion.

On the lake, winds stay light and manageable through the afternoon, waves a foot or under, water's a comfortable 73. But south wind builds to 15-20 knots overnight as the next system moves in, so tonight's not the night for an evening paddle. The bigger story is Tuesday into Wednesday, when the forecasters are increasingly confident a slow-moving system parks over us with heavier downpours and a real risk of localized flooding, especially on saturated ground. Good window for the water and any plans today is before 4 or 5 this evening; after that, keep an eye on the sky and don't be surprised by a quick, heavy hit.
